metadata.selection_basis: Selected from 232 Phase 1 candidates scored by score_keywords.py against allocation.json tier budgets (10 A / 6 B / 4 C). Every selection verified NOT to duplicate any of the 50 already-tracked keywords.
metadata.intent_mix_note: The skill's ~60/25/15 transactional/informational/comparison constraint could NOT be verified from scored data: score_keywords.py classified all 232 candidates as intent='informational', including plainly commercial terms like 'caterers melbourne' and 'corporate catering melbourne cbd'. This is a classifier artefact, not a property of the pool. Intent balance was therefore judged manually from SERP composition (local_pack present on 17 of 20 selections) and CPC (14 of 20 above $2.50, peaking at $29.76) — both of which indicate commercial intent dominates. Flagged rather than silently claimed as satisfied.

strategic_narratives.title: Commercial service pages rank 20-53 while blog posts rank 6-11 — the site structure is inverted
strategic_narratives.summary: The homepage absorbs 174,106 impressions at position 15.2, but the pages that should convert sit far below it: /corporate-catering/ at 52.6 (10,912 impressions, 14 clicks), /corporate-catering/conference-meeting/ at 49.2, /event-catering/ at 46.3, /corporate-catering/drop-off/ at 39.9, /corporate-catering/cocktail-party/ at 28.8. Meanwhile informational blog posts rank 5.9-11.1. The 50 already-tracked keywords point at those weak commercial pages, which is why they underperform (corporate catering melbourne pos 16.8, corporate catering pos 22.8, cocktail catering pos 37.0). Fixing those pages is the single highest-value action available to this site and is OUTSIDE the scope of a keyword package. These 20 new keywords were deliberately weighted toward demand where GSC already proves position 4-15 traction, or toward service lines with no page at all, precisely to avoid inheriting the position-50 problem.

strategic_narratives.title: Three Q10 service lines carry real demand and zero keyword coverage
strategic_narratives.summary: Morning & Afternoon Teas (afternoon tea catering 720/mo, catering morning tea 390/mo), Weddings (wedding catering melbourne 480/mo, already ranking 7.6 on 1,728 impressions) and At-Home Meals (home catering melbourne already ranking 4.3) are all named service lines in questionnaire Q10 with zero keywords among the tracked 50 and, in the case of At-Home and the teas, no landing page either. All four of the client's own Q11 keyword preferences are already tracked or near-duplicated, so client-stated priorities were NOT treated as a to-do list.

strategic_narratives.title: University, government and council segments have no measurable search demand
strategic_narratives.summary: Questionnaire Q9 names universities, government bodies and councils as a key customer group and Q7 documents genuine dispatch specialisation for those sites (loading docks, security procedures, goods lifts, restricted vehicle access). DataForSEO returned NO measurable volume for 'university catering melbourne', 'government catering melbourne', 'meal boxes catering' or 'individual meal boxes catering'. These segments are won through tenders and relationships, not search, so no keyword slots were spent on them. This should be stated plainly to the client rather than papered over.

general_keywords.reasoning: The largest untracked term in the entire dataset at 2,900/mo, KD 24, CPC $5.24 — and the client already sits at GSC position 5.6 on 694 impressions without ever targeting it. 'Caterers' outperforms the tracked 'catering companies' form by 6x on volume (2,900 vs 480), which is why the tracked 50 miss it. Phase 3c shows the top 3 are thecateringcompany.com.au, devouritcatering.com.au and elizabethandrews.com.au — all three direct Melbourne caterers, no directories, so this is a winnable head SERP rather than a HiPages-style aggregator fight. Local pack is present, which the client's 6,000 deliveries/year and physical Melbourne facility support. KD 24 exactly matches client DA 24, making this the hardest justified selection in the package: achievable at top 5 within 6-9 months given the existing position-5.6 baseline.

Weddings are an explicit Q10 service line ('Functions & Event Catering — Private Parties, Weddings, & Cocktail/Canape Events') with ZERO keywords among the 50 tracked — the single largest coverage hole in the package. 480/mo, KD 21 against client DA 24, CPC $4.39, with strong seasonality (peaks of 880 in both March and September). The client already earns 1,728 GSC impressions at position 7.6 with no wedding page whatsoever; the traffic is landing on /wedding-menu-inspiration-create-an-unforgettable-dining-experience/, a blog post pulling 4,042 impressions at position 10.4. That is proven topical authority with no commercial page behind it — build the service page and internally link the existing blog to it. Phase 3c top 3 are cloverfood.com.au, peterrowland.com.au and easyweddings.com.au: one directory (easyweddings) in the top 3 is displaceable with a proper service page, and Peter Rowland is a premium incumbent the client's $20M public liability and full-service staffing offer can credibly compete against.

secondaries.keyword: how much does wedding catering cost per person in australia

general_keywords.content_type: Service page (same page as wedding catering melbourne — dual-target)
general_keywords.reasoning: Retained alongside 'wedding catering melbourne' as a deliberate exception to the one-keyword-per-topic rule, because the entire wedding line is untracked rather than being an already-covered topic with variants. The 'caterers' form already ranks at GSC position 3.7 on 915 impressions — materially better than the 'catering' form's 7.6 — so a single wedding service page dual-targeting both forms captures a near-page-one position immediately while the harder form matures. 480/mo, KD 21 vs client DA 24. Phase 3c returns four PAA questions on this SERP ('What is the cheapest way to feed 100 people at a wedding?', 'How much does wedding catering cost per person in Australia?') which map directly onto FAQ schema — and Q14 confirms the client publishes no fixed price list, so a transparent per-person cost band on this page would answer the dominant buyer question competitors leave open.

secondaries.keyword: what is the cheapest way to feed 100 people at a wedding

general_keywords.reasoning: Bare-term selection justified on Phase 3c evidence: top_3 for this SERP is catering.soulorigin.com.au, missmaud.com.au and fabulouscatering.com.au — 3 of 3 .com.au, confirming an AU-dominated commercial SERP with no international or jobs-board contamination. 1,600/mo at KD 7 is the best volume-to-difficulty ratio in the entire selection, well inside client DA 24. gaps.json classes this EXISTS_NEEDS_OPTIMISATION mapped to /corporate-catering/cocktail-party/, but that page currently ranks 28.8 on 14,279 impressions and converts 36 clicks — the mapping is weak and the page is mis-scoped for a generic food-catering query. Recommend re-pointing this term at a broader services hub rather than the cocktail-party child page. Local pack present; four PAA questions available ('What is the cheapest food to cater a party?', 'How much should it cost to feed 20 people?') that Q14's quote-based model can answer with a headcount calculator no competitor in this top 3 currently offers.

secondaries.keyword: how much should it cost to feed 20 people

general_keywords.reasoning: 260/mo at CPC $8.31 — the third-highest CPC in the selection, signalling strong commercial intent — with the client already at current_position 13 and GSC position 5.0 on 503 impressions. This is the clearest USP-to-keyword match in the whole package: Q7 and Q9 document a dispatch team with detailed working knowledge of Melbourne CBD loading docks, security procedures, goods lifts, restricted vehicle access and multiple reception areas, plus multiple daily delivery runs 7:30am-5:30pm per Q14. None of the Phase 3c top 3 (earlcanteen.com.au, cateringproject.com.au, briskcatering.com.au) can claim that operational depth on a page. Local pack present. A CBD page that names specific building-access capability converts a logistics advantage into a ranking asset.

general_keywords.content_type: Service page (new — remap off the office page)
general_keywords.reasoning: 260/mo, KD 10 (well inside DA 24), current_position 14 and 1,567 GSC impressions at position 5.1 — a textbook striking-distance term. The critical finding is the mapping: gaps.json currently maps this to /corporate-catering/office/, a corporate page ranking 20.0. Every 'party' keyword among the tracked 50 is corporate-scoped (Office Party Catering, Corporate Party Catering, Cocktail Party Catering), which means private-party demand is being funnelled to a workplace page and losing the query. Q9 explicitly names private individuals hosting birthdays, anniversaries and retirement parties as an ideal customer group. Phase 3c top 3 (cateringbychefs.com.au, fabulouscatering.com.au, devouritcatering.com.au) are all direct caterers with no directory presence, and local pack is present. A dedicated non-corporate party page resolves the mismatch.

210/mo, KD 16 against DA 24, current_position 12 and 715 GSC impressions at position 8.1 — already page-one-adjacent with no page targeting it. Distinct from 'party catering melbourne' by venue rather than by modifier: this is catering delivered into a private residence, which Q9 names directly ('private individuals hosting intimate gatherings') and which Q8's full-service proposition addresses — one team handling food, beverages, equipment and staffing is materially more valuable in a home with no commercial kitchen than in an office. Phase 3c top 3 are thecateringcompany.com.au, cateringbychefs.com.au and oliveandthymecatering.com.au, all direct caterers, local pack present. Retained as the third party-cluster term because it targets a separate landing page and buyer context, not a wording variant.

Modest at 70/mo but KD 0 and 616 GSC impressions already at position 14 with no page — the demand is arriving and being absorbed by the homepage. Q9 names birthday parties as an ideal customer occasion, and the existing blog /from-weddings-to-baby-showers-catering-for-milestone-celebrations/ pulls 1,227 impressions at position 16.5, proving the client already has topical relevance for milestone celebrations with nothing commercial behind it. Selected over higher-volume party variants because it is a distinct buying occasion with its own landing intent rather than a wording variant, and because KD 0 against DA 24 makes it near-certain to rank. Volume caveat stated openly: this is the lowest-volume selection in the package and is justified on zero difficulty plus existing impression evidence, not on headline volume.

140/mo at KD 0 with CPC $3.53. Chosen as a USP play rather than a volume play: Q16 documents HACCP-based allergen management as a formal, audited procedure — hazard identification, allergen controls, traceability, documented corrective actions — which is a genuine E-E-A-T asset for dietary queries that a competitor asserting 'we cater for vegans' cannot match. The existing blog /dietary-friendly-catering-how-to-include-everyone-at-the-table/ already earns 973 impressions at position 13.2, confirming topical traction with no service page. GSC impressions for this exact term are effectively nil (1), so this is a demand-creation play on measured DataForSEO volume rather than a striking-distance win — stated plainly rather than dressed up. Pair with gluten free catering melbourne on a single dietary hub page.

110/mo, KD 0, CPC $5.11 — notably higher CPC than the vegan term, indicating stronger commercial urgency, and unlike the vegan term it has real GSC evidence at position 13.1 on 57 impressions, making it the stronger of the two dietary picks. Same USP foundation: Q16's documented allergen management and staff hygiene training is exactly the assurance a buyer catering for a coeliac guest is searching for, and Q15's $20M public liability cover is a credibility signal for risk-averse corporate bookers. Shares the /dietary-catering-melbourne/ hub with the vegan term to avoid thin duplicate pages, with distinct H2 sections and separate FAQ schema per dietary requirement.

Bare-term selection justified on Phase 3c evidence: top_3 is cateringproject.com.au, feedwell.com.au and maryeatscake.com.au — 3 of 3 .com.au, an AU-dominated SERP. At 720/mo this is the highest-volume term in Tier B and the flagship of an entire Q10 service line ('Morning & Afternoon Teas, Lunches, and Multi-Course Plated Boardroom Meals') that has ZERO representation among the 50 tracked keywords and no landing page. Local pack is present and AI Overview is present — the AIO makes structured, answerable content (per-head quantities, menu formats, lead times) a citation opportunity rather than a threat. Q13's 6,000 deliveries and functions per year plus Q14's multiple daily delivery runs directly support the recurring, time-critical nature of workplace tea catering. Note the Melbourne-qualified form measures only 50/mo, so the unqualified term is deliberately chosen as the primary with the geo form as a secondary.

Bare-term selection justified on Phase 3c evidence: top_3 is catering.soulorigin.com.au, catering.let-them-eat.com.au and saycheesebne.com — AU-dominated (the .com is a Brisbane operator), no international contamination. 390/mo at KD 0 with CPC $6.63, the fourth-highest CPC in the package, indicating workplace buyers with budget. Completes the Morning & Afternoon Teas Q10 line alongside the afternoon-tea term on a shared hub page. The Melbourne-qualified variant measures just 50/mo versus 390/mo unqualified, so targeting the unqualified head with Melbourne context in the on-page copy captures materially more demand — the client's delivery radius per Q14 is metropolitan Melbourne, so geographic relevance is established by the local pack and page content rather than by the query string.

480/mo at CPC $9.63 — the second-highest CPC in the package — with the client already at GSC position 4.9 on 440 impressions. Deliberately a CBD-qualified corporate term rather than another generic corporate head: 16 of the 50 tracked keywords are already generic corporate variants and their landing pages rank 20-53, so adding more generic corporate terms would compound an optimisation problem. The CBD qualifier is where the client's documented operational advantage lives (Q7: loading docks, security procedures, goods lifts, restricted vehicle access across CBD corporate offices and government buildings). Phase 3c top 3 are elizabethandrews.com.au, briskcatering.com.au and cateringproject.com.au — direct competitors, no directories, local pack present. KD 22 sits just under client DA 24.

CPC $29.76 — by a wide margin the highest commercial signal in the entire 232-candidate pool, more than triple the next-highest term — on 140/mo at KD 13, comfortably inside client DA 24. The client already holds GSC position 7.4 on 942 impressions. The tracked 50 include 'Office Catering Melbourne' but not the CBD-qualified form, and the existing /corporate-catering/office/ page ranks 20.0 on 2,574 impressions, so a CBD child page both captures the higher-value query and gives the underperforming parent an internal-link boost. Q7's dispatch specialisation in CBD goods lifts and reception-area logistics is the precise differentiator for recurring office catering, where reliability of delivery time matters more than menu novelty. Phase 3c top 3: urbanfoodies.com.au, briskcatering.com.au, elizabethandrews.com.au — direct caterers, local pack present, four PAA questions available for FAQ schema.

CPC $11.13 on only 90/mo — the third-highest CPC in the package and a clear signal that the buyers behind this query convert. Client is already at GSC position 3.5 on 567 impressions and gaps.json maps it cleanly to the existing /corporate-catering/lunch-dinner/ page, making this pure optimisation rather than new build. It also directly serves the client's own Q11 stated preference ('Lunch catering in Melbourne'), which is NOT present in the tracked 50 in this unqualified-service form — the tracked set only carries 'Corporate Lunch Catering Melbourne' and 'Office Lunch Catering Melbourne'. Phase 3c top 3 are urbanfoodies.com.au, earlcanteen.com.au and elizabethandrews.com.au with local pack present. Low volume is accepted here because the page already exists, the position is already 3.5, and the CPC proves commercial value — the marginal cost of targeting it is close to zero.

110/mo at KD 0 and CPC $5.32, with 444 GSC impressions already accruing at position 17 and no page targeting it. Breakfast is entirely absent from the tracked 50 despite being the natural companion to the client's 7:30am delivery start documented in Q5 and Q14 — the operational capability to deliver a staffed breakfast into a CBD office before 9am is a genuine constraint most caterers cannot meet, and Q7's refrigerated-vehicle and temperature-control procedures make early-morning cold-chain delivery defensible. Phase 3c top 3 are terrortwilight.com.au, devouritcatering.com.au and cateringproject.com.au, local pack present, four PAA questions including portion-size queries that suit a per-head planning table.

general_keywords.reasoning: 260/mo at KD 0 — zero difficulty against client DA 24 — with current_position 20 and 1,041 GSC impressions at position 9.4. The tracked 50 contain only 'Cocktail Finger Food Catering', leaving the far more commonly searched standalone form uncovered. gaps.json maps it to /corporate-catering/cocktail-party/, a page carrying 14,279 impressions but ranking 28.8, so this is a high-leverage optimisation: the page already attracts enormous impression volume and simply is not converting position. The supporting blog /cold-vs-hot-finger-foods-which-is-best-for-your-next-event/ ranks 8.0 on 1,794 impressions and should be internally linked into it. Phase 3c top 3 include cheapfingerfoodcatering.com.au and thepartyfoodshop.com.au — budget-positioned operators the client's chef-prepared, Q18 'premium quality' positioning can differentiate against on quality rather than price. Four PAA questions available on quantities per guest.

general_keywords.content_type: Service page (new — replaces PDF as the ranking asset)
general_keywords.reasoning: 110/mo at KD 0 and CPC $6.68, with the client already at GSC position 5.8 on 519 impressions. The standout evidence is that a PDF is doing the ranking: black_truffle_2020_spring_summer_canape_menu.pdf earns 1,174 impressions at position 10.3 and 21 clicks. A six-year-old PDF outranking the site's HTML for a commercial query is a clear structural miss — an indexable canape service page with the menu as on-page HTML would inherit that demand and be optimisable, linkable and convertible in a way a PDF never is. Canapes are named explicitly in Q10's food packages line and carry the lowest competition index (56) of any term probed in Phase 0. Note this term was not covered by the Phase 3c probe set, but it is geo-qualified so the bare-term SERP rule does not apply.

general_keywords.content_type: Service page (new — At Home Meals hub)
general_keywords.reasoning: The single most complete blind spot on the site: 'At Home Meals / Re-heat Meals' is a named Q10 service line with zero keywords among the tracked 50 AND no page in the sitemap, yet the client already ranks GSC position 4.3 on 276 impressions purely off homepage authority. 90/mo at KD 11 against DA 24. Q9 describes the exact buyer — 'residential customers who want restaurant-quality, chef-prepared meals to re-heat at home, saving them time in the kitchen' — and Q7's documented temperature-control and refrigerated-vehicle procedures are precisely the reassurance a re-heat product needs. Ranking top-5 on a service the business sells but has never built a page for is the clearest quick win in the package: the demand and the authority already exist, only the page is missing.

secondaries.keyword: restaurant quality meals at home melbourne

general_keywords.content_type: Service page (same At Home Meals hub)
general_keywords.reasoning: 170/mo at KD 0 — higher volume than the 'home catering' form and zero difficulty against DA 24. Completes the Q10 'At Home Meals / Re-heat Meals' line by capturing the product-led half of the query space: 'home catering' expresses a service brought to a home, whereas 'ready made meals' expresses a product collected or delivered for re-heating, which is exactly what Q9 describes the client selling to residential customers. Shares the /at-home-catering-melbourne/ hub with 'home catering melbourne' under distinct H2 sections to avoid thin duplicate pages. Selected in place of 'grazing table melbourne' (210/mo, KD 0) after Phase 3c showed that SERP has NO local pack and is held by three dedicated grazing specialists — grazebysteph.com.au, grazenthings.com.au, melbournegrazing.com.au — making it a specialist niche a full-service caterer would be poorly positioned to take, whereas re-heat meals maps to a service the client already provides.
